runs.text: . The value in the question appears only as the top of the first range they tested: the boronic-acid CD signal of BA@L-HGNRs redispersed in NH4HCO3 buffer rose sharply

runs.quote: as the 4-MPBA concentration was tuned from 0 to 120 μM

1. Stability: in time-dependent CD and UV–vis tests,

runs.quote: the 165 μM 4-MPBA-derived BA@L-HGNRs showing exceptional spectral stability during the entire monitoring process

runs.text:
. They read this as proof that the boronic-acid coating improved how well the particles stayed dispersed in the buffer.
2. CD intensity:

up to 225 μM resulted in only marginal changes in the CD signal

The underlying goal was good dispersion. The authors note that how BA@L-HGNRs disperse in the buffer depends on BA surface coverage, which

runs.quote: further affects their interfacial interaction with bacterial surfaces

rendered:
The question doesn't match the paper. The authors did not pick that concentration as the optimum. They chose a 4-MPBA concentra-tion of 165 μM was chosen as the optimized condition for all subsequent experiments[1]. The value in the question appears only as the top of the first range they tested: the boronic-acid CD signal of BA@L-HGNRs redispersed in NH4HCO3 buffer rose sharply as the 4-MPBA concentration was tuned from 0 to 120 μM[2].

They give these reasons for the concentration they settled on:
1. Stability: in time-dependent CD and UV–vis tests, the 165 μM 4-MPBA-derived BA@L-HGNRs showing exceptional spectral stability during the entire monitoring process[3]. They read this as proof that the boronic-acid coating improved how well the particles stayed dispersed in the buffer.
2. CD intensity: The CD intensity reached its maximum at 165 μM, after which it exhibited a slight decrease at higher concentrations[4]. Going higher, up to 225 μM resulted in only marginal changes in the CD signal[5].

The underlying goal was good dispersion. The authors note that how BA@L-HGNRs disperse in the buffer depends on BA surface coverage, which further affects their interfacial interaction with bacterial surfaces[6]. The concentration in the question also appears as the top of the cysteine range tested when making L-HGNRs. There, the optimum cysteine level was a lower value, not the top of that range.[7]
